subject: PoC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@acme-corp.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, lauren_bishop, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: PoC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp

Hi Sam / Olivia 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Recap:
- We discussed three deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest to validate), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs for production throughput), and Private VPC/on-prem (for regulated workloads).
- Acme's initial priorities: data isolation, KMS integration, and predictable latency for high-volume inference.

Recommended PoC approach:
1) Short Hosted API spike (1 week) to validate model quality and basic latency/cost assumptions using sanitized sample data.
2) Parallel evaluation of Private VPC requirements (security review + KMS integration) with a goal decision at the end of week 4.

Success criteria (draft):
- 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for 1k concurrent users (sample workload)
- End-to-end throughput target: X requests/minute (we'll quantify once we have sample traffic)
- KMS integration for encryption-at-rest and in-transit verified by your security team
- No PHI transmitted in Hosted spike; Private VPC validated for sensitive data flows

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): confirm stakeholders and provide sample dataset (sanitized) + IP allowlist for test endpoints
- Week 1: Hosted spike (model tuning + quick perf tests)
- Week 2-4: Private VPC onboarding (security review, initial KMS tests, connectivity)

Attachments: redwood-poc-trial-plan.pdf (attached) with an outline of milestones, required access, and checklist.

Could you confirm the stakeholders we should loop in (security, infra, procurement) and whether you want us to prioritize the Private VPC track over the Hosted spike? If you prefer to skip Hosted entirely due to compliance, we can focus resources on a fast Private-only path.

Next step: I propose a 30-min follow-up early next week to align on stakeholders and sign off on the PoC scope. Does Tuesday 6/22 at 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-poc-trial-plan.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sam Green <sam.green@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-21T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp

Thanks Ben  good summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Compliance: Acme handles regulated customer PII. Our security and compliance teams are strongly leaning toward a Private VPC solution for any PoC that touches real customer data. If the Hosted spike can be executed with fully sanitized synthetic data, we are OK running it, but it cannot contain PHI/PII.
- Stakeholders to include: Olivia Chen (CTO), Rajiv Kumar (Head of Security, rajiv.kumar@acme-corp.com), and Procurement (procurement@acme-corp.com).
- Evidence required for Private VPC track: SOC 2 report, summary of network isolation architecture, KMS/HSM integration docs, and a short runbook for customer-managed keys.

We'd prefer to prioritize the Private VPC track, but are open to a quick Hosted spike if Marissa confirms it can be done safely with synthetic data. Please schedule the follow-up with Rajiv and Olivia  Rajiv is only available afternoons PT.

Best,
Sam Green
Head of Product, Acme Corp
sam.green@acme-corp.com

Hi Sam / Olivia 

Thanks  wanted to add a technical proposal to Ben's commercial plan so you can see how we'd run both tracks if you choose to proceed.

Proposed technical PoC (two-track, parallel):
- Track A (Hosted spike, 1 week):
  - Purpose: quick validation of model quality, prompt templates, and baseline latency using synthetic/sanitized traffic.
  - Deliverables: sample inference pipeline config, 90-min perf run with synthetic load, latency/throughput report.
  - Data access: sanitized dataset only; no PHI/PII allowed.

- Track B (Private VPC evaluation, 2-4 weeks):
  - Purpose: validate networking, KMS integration, audit logs, and production-like throughput.
  - Deliverables: VPC deployment plan, KMS integration test, audit-log collection test, runbook for customer-managed keys, and a final run at target concurrency.
  - Required access: temporary VPN/IP allowlist, service account for S3 access to sample data, contact for your infra/SRE (for routing & peering).

Milestones by week:
- Week 0: NDA/compliance paperwork + access provisioning (procurement + security)
- Week 1: Hosted spike + initial perf report
- Week 2: Private VPC onboarding + KMS smoke test
- Week 3-4: Throughput validation and handoff notes

Success criteria (technical):
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 250ms under defined concurrency
- End-to-end throughput meets target requests/minute within a 10% margin
- KMS integration using customer-managed keys verified end-to-end
- Audit logs captured and delivered to your SIEM (sample events)

If you prefer Private-first, we can move resources to accelerate Track B and do the Hosted spike as a limited synthetic test only. I've attached the detailed trial plan (redwood-poc-trial-plan.pdf) with the checklist and a short access matrix.

Please confirm:
1) Which track to prioritize (Private-first vs Parallel)
2) Primary infra/security contact and an email we can use to request a short onboarding call
3) Any mandatory compliance docs we need to share up-front (SOC2, HIPAA BAAs, etc.)

Happy to jump on a technical 30-min call with Rajiv and your infra team  afternoons PT work best for us.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

We want to prioritize the Private VPC track given the sensitivity of the data. We are OK with a limited Hosted spike using synthetic data only, but only if it won't delay Private onboarding.

- Procurement will review the trial plan and confirm NDAs and any legal templates; procurement@acme-corp.com will pick up next steps on contracts.
